title: One-time genomic cure of severe monogenic skin disease through the epidermal stem-cell compartment

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a one-time genetic treatment that restores function in diseased skin by correcting enough of the long-lived epidermal stem cells that continually renew it. Their descendants would retain the restored function as older surface cells are shed. The intended result is sustained benefit in treated tissue without repeated corrective treatment. Durable local restoration already has clinical precedent; the broader capability would make that outcome reliable across different disease genes and more difficult tissue settings.

Genetic correction can take different forms. Integrating gene replacement adds a functional gene to stem cells, whereas precise editing changes a disease-causing sequence or introduces corrective DNA at a targeted location. Both could satisfy this concept if they produce durable, functional stem-cell populations with acceptable safety. Ex vivo treatment corrects cells outside the body before transplanting epidermal sheets; future in vivo approaches would need to reach and correct the relevant stem cells within the patient. Precise editing is therefore a possible route, rather than a mandatory feature of every qualifying treatment.

Scope synthesis: the proposed advance extends beyond a successful graft for one epidermolysis bullosa subtype. It seeks convincing results across distinct causal genes and includes restoration at a difficult site, such as mucosa or intact but malfunctioning epidermis. Severe ichthyoses and xeroderma pigmentosum are proposed applications; the supplied clinical evidence concerns epidermolysis bullosa. The concept does not require a single vector for every mutation, and it does not include using corrected skin as a factory for systemic drugs.

significance.text: Severe epidermolysis bullosa causes persistent skin fragility, wounds and extracutaneous disease. Correcting the regenerative source of the epidermis could sustain local tissue function despite continual cell turnover, reducing dependence on repeated corrective gene delivery. The revolutionary extension would be reliable, reproducible restoration across diseases and tissue settings, building on the substantial local benefits already demonstrated by stem-cell grafting.

Benefits at mucosal or intact-skin sites remain conditional on successful delivery, stem-cell correction or engraftment, and persistence at those sites. In particular, the February 2026 review identifies inaccessible mucosa, including the esophagus and gastrointestinal tract, as a major unresolved target. Systemic delivery might eventually expand treatment reach, but the review treats delivery to internal tissues as a development requirement, not an established substitute for local grafting.

Impact synthesis: sustained function in treated skin would not by itself establish whole-body correction, elimination of extracutaneous disease, or freedom from all subsequent care. Successful treatment of two diseases would demonstrate broader applicability, not universal mutation coverage. Nor would it establish zero genomic risk. Extension to ichthyoses or xeroderma pigmentosum could be consequential, but the supplied EB-focused evidence does not establish those diseases' current treatment status or demonstrate their correction.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is reliable correction of enough long-lived, regenerative epidermal stem cells across distinct disease genes and tissue settings. Correcting short-lived cells alone cannot establish a persistently corrected epidermis. Koller's 2023 editorial offers an insufficient number of corrected epidermal stem cells as a possible explanation for limited maintenance in some earlier recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa graft studies. That is a hypothesis about particular outcomes, rather than proof that inadequate correction of holoclones explains every graft failure.

Delivery and tissue occupation remain separate engineering barriers. Non-integrating topical B-VEC requires repeated application; integrating stem-cell grafts can provide durable local benefit but require cell preparation and transplantation. The February 2026 review describes EB genome editing as predominantly ex vivo and preclinical, and reports that genetic correction of inaccessible gastrointestinal and esophageal mucosa had not been demonstrated. Proposed extension to intact malfunctioning epidermis adds a further requirement: corrected stem cells must become established and persist in that setting. The supplied evidence does not establish a general quantitative comparison of its difficulty with open-wound grafting.

Genomic safety and consistency across causal genes also remain barriers. Editing can produce unintended changes at the intended target as well as elsewhere in the genome, while integrating vectors require assessment of insertion-related risks. The 2026 review describes variable efficacy between loci and the potential cost and time required for mutation-specific therapies. Emerging whole-gene integration approaches may broaden treatment within certain subtypes, but they do not establish one universally applicable correction method.

Remaining uncertainty: immune responses to a restored protein are a relevant question for extending treatment across genodermatoses, but the supplied texts do not establish their general frequency, severity or unresolved status across such a platform. This concern should remain an explicit subject for investigation rather than a categorical claim that restored-protein immunity prevents durable correction.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies Hirsch and colleagues' 2017 LAMB3 junctional epidermolysis bullosa case as a major demonstration of extensive epidermal regeneration. Koller's June 2023 editorial describes retroviral transgenic epidermal stem-cell grafts covering approximately 80% of a child's body surface area over three surgeries, and reports effectiveness eight years after treatment. These details are retained as the editorial's account, as characterized by the supplied review; the underlying Nature report was not independently inspected in that review. The result establishes an important local regenerative capability in a particular disease setting, rather than reproducibility across multiple causal genes or tissue types.

Historical limitations in recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa graft maintenance should be read alongside later long-term benefit. The February 2026 review reports that, after a mean follow-up of 5.9 years, 70% of treated sites across seven RDEB patients showed at least 50% wound healing. This is substantial evidence of durable local benefit. It is neither evidence of complete healing at every site nor a demonstration of whole-body correction, but it prevents earlier graft limitations from being mistaken for the current limit of the entire approach.

Vyjuvek, beremagene geperpavec or B-VEC, is an approved topical HSV-1 therapy that delivers COL7A1. Koller's 2023 editorial summarizes complete wound healing as 67% with B-VEC versus 22% with placebo at six months. The February 2026 review separately reports B-VEC wound closure of 71% at three months and 67% at six months. Those time-point percentages should not be converted into a claim that an identical 67% of wounds healed by month three and continuously remained healed through month six. The supplied summaries do not provide the wound-level evidence needed for that interpretation. B-VEC requires repeated application and does not permanently correct the epidermal stem-cell compartment.

Stanford's June 23, 2025 news release reports FDA approval on April 29, 2025 of its gene-corrected RDEB graft therapy, identifies the VIITAL publication as prademagene zamikeracel, and describes results in 11 patients with 43 wound pairs. At week 24, at least 50% healing occurred in 81% of treated wounds versus 16% of control wounds; complete healing occurred in 16% versus none. The February 2026 review identifies the approved therapy as Zevaskyn. These results concern locally applied epidermal sheets for chronic wounds and do not demonstrate mucosal or whole-body correction.

The VIITAL figures above come from the retained Stanford news release, not direct inspection of the trial paper. The supplied Lancet abstract URL was not captured. Earlier notes gave exact counts of 35 of 43 treated wounds and 7 of 43 controls reaching at least half healing; those counts are consistent with the reported rounded percentages but were not directly printed in the retained texts described by the review. The percentages and denominator are therefore the supported quantitative account here, while the exact counts remain unverified in this record.

The February 2026 CRISPR review was available in full HTML and PDF according to the supplied evidence review, correcting the earlier characterization of abstract-only access. Its broad statement about the absence of a permanent treatment must be interpreted alongside documented durable local graft benefits: the remaining gap is a broadly applicable cure, not the absence of any lasting correction. It documents continuing delivery, stem-cell targeting and genomic-safety barriers. The supplied record does not establish comprehensive coverage of developments after February 2026 through November 1, 2026; the later source-retrieval date alone does not resolve that gap.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: a single corrective intervention, ex vivo or in vivo, would produce at least three years of stable restored function without further corrective treatment in treated tissue for two severe genodermatoses involving different causal genes. Molecular evidence would show that corrected epidermal stem-cell clones persist and continue to supply functional tissue. At least one demonstration would include mucosa or an intact-skin disease such as a severe ichthyosis. These are proposed evaluative thresholds, not established clinical or regulatory standards.
completion_criteria.label: Single intervention restores three-year function across two genetically distinct genodermatoses

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and functional evidence: results should recur in independent patients and separately prepared treatments, with transparent reporting of the treated area, causal variants, successful and failed sites, and the functional outcome relevant to each disease. Persistent corrective DNA or protein expression alone would be insufficient without sustained tissue function. Follow-up should distinguish renewed corrective treatment from other supportive care. A successful single junctional EB graft and repeatedly dosed wound therapy remain important achieved components, but would not complete this broader demonstration.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained tissue function recurs across independent patients and treatment preparations

completion_criteria.text: Proposed safety evidence: assessment should match the intervention and include unintended on-target and off-target changes for editing, insertion-related risks for integrating vectors, and longitudinal evidence about the behavior of corrected clones. Delivery complications and clinically relevant responses to treatment or restored protein should also be evaluated. These proposed assessments respond to documented genomic and delivery concerns; the supplied evidence does not establish a universal numerical threshold for acceptable risk.
completion_criteria.label: Intervention-specific genomic risks, clonal behavior and clinical safety are assessed

completion_criteria.text: Interpretive boundary of the proposal: three years would establish durability over that interval, not lifelong cure. Success across two causal genes and selected tissue sites would establish demonstrated breadth, not literal universality. Claims should remain bounded by the treated area and tissue type, the patients studied, follow-up duration and the genomic risks the measurements can detect. Whole-body benefit, extracutaneous correction and further disease applications would each require additional evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Claims remain bounded by demonstrated durability, breadth and detectable risks

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis — DER-01, Clinical restoration of a complete human skin organ: both concepts involve regenerative cells and tissue engineering. DER-02 focuses on durable genetic restoration through the epidermal stem-cell compartment; that does not by itself establish restoration of a complete skin organ with all its structures and functions.

Roster-based synthesis — DER-04, Programmable passage of macromolecules and gene editors across intact stratum corneum: improved passage could enable an in vivo route for DER-02. Crossing the surface barrier would still leave stem-cell targeting, sufficient correction, persistence and genomic safety to demonstrate. DER-02 could also succeed through ex vivo grafting without solving intact-skin delivery.

Roster-based synthesis — DER-05, Epidermal DNA repair sufficient to prevent ultraviolet-driven skin cancer, and DER-06, Therapeutic reset of the mutant epidermal field: these overlap with DER-02 in durable changes to epidermal cell populations. DER-05 targets prevention of ultraviolet-driven cancer, while DER-06 targets an established mutant field. A proposed xeroderma pigmentosum application could connect DER-02 with DER-05, but correcting an inherited defect would not automatically establish cancer prevention or removal of pre-existing mutant clones.

Roster-based synthesis — DER-03, Antigen-selective erasure of pathogenic cutaneous immune memory, and DER-07, A skin-origin intervention that prevents atopic dermatitis and the atopic march: these address immune memory or prevention of an inflammatory disease trajectory. DER-02 instead addresses inherited defects through genetically corrected epidermal stem cells. Improved local skin function would not by itself demonstrate either selective immune-memory erasure or prevention of the atopic march.

Roster-based synthesis — DER-08, Reconstitution of melanocyte stem cells where the follicular reservoir is gone: both depend on establishing a durable regenerative cell population, but they target different compartments. Persistent corrected epidermal stem cells do not establish that a lost melanocyte stem-cell reservoir has been rebuilt.

Roster-based synthesis — DER-09, Durable regenerative closure of diabetic foot ulcers after ischemia and pressure are treated, and DER-10, In situ reversal of established keloids and pathological cutaneous scars: all three concern durable tissue improvement, but their causal targets differ. DER-02 corrects an inherited epidermal defect; DER-09 addresses ulcer regeneration after vascular and mechanical contributors are treated; DER-10 addresses established pathological scarring. EB wound-healing results cannot establish either diabetic-ulcer regeneration or scar reversal.

change_log.reason: Durable local stem-cell graft benefits already exist; the hypothetical advance is their reliable extension.

change_log.change: Made integrating gene replacement and precise editing distinct qualifying routes.
change_log.reason: The original completion proposal permits both, whereas other wording incorrectly implied that precise editing was mandatory.

change_log.change: Replaced the categorical holoclone-failure explanation with a hypothesis about particular earlier RDEB graft outcomes.
change_log.reason: Koller presents insufficient corrected stem cells as a possible explanation, not a universal causal finding.

change_log.change: Added the longer-term RDEB result of at least 50% wound healing at 70% of treated sites across seven patients after a mean 5.9 years.
change_log.reason: The later review materially qualifies the earlier account of limited graft maintenance.

change_log.change: Separated B-VEC's reported three-month and six-month outcomes and removed the inferred continuous-healing trajectory.
change_log.reason: The supplied secondary summaries report different time-point figures without establishing wound-level continuity.

change_log.change: Used VIITAL percentages with the 43-pair denominator and identified the Stanford release as the outcome source.
change_log.reason: The Lancet artifact was unavailable, and exact counts were not directly printed in the retained evidence described by the review.

change_log.change: Corrected the 2026 review's access description from abstract-only to full HTML and PDF.
change_log.reason: The validated review identifies complete retained texts and substantive passages beyond the abstract.

change_log.change: Qualified blanket language about no permanent treatment and distinguished local benefit from a broadly applicable cure.
change_log.reason: An unqualified formulation would erase documented durable correction.

change_log.change: Removed universal-vector and zero-off-target-risk requirements; retained intact-skin treatment and additional diseases as proposed extensions.
change_log.reason: Those universal requirements were unsupported and unnecessary, while broader applications remain part of the concept's intended scope.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed safety evidence to include unintended on-target changes and insertion-related risks, and bounded the three-year criterion.
change_log.reason: Safety must cover both permitted correction routes, and finite follow-up cannot prove lifelong cure.

change_log.change: Added explicit reproducibility proposals, practical boundaries and distinctions from every other supplied roster entry.
change_log.reason: Completion requires interpretable breadth and repeatability, while overlapping innovations retain separate identities.

unresolved_issues: Comprehensive coverage of developments after February 2026 through November 1, 2026 is not established by the supplied freshness record.
The exact VIITAL counts of 35 of 43 treated wounds and 7 of 43 controls remain unverified in the retained texts; the underlying Lancet artifact was not captured.

The attribution and chronology of the eight-year follow-up warrant clarification: the supplied materials associate that duration with Koller's account of the child graft case while also identifying the landmark report as published in 2017. The editorial's reported duration is preserved without an invented resolution.
The supplied B-VEC summaries do not resolve wound-level continuity between the three-month and six-month outcomes.
The evidence does not establish correction of inaccessible gastrointestinal or esophageal mucosa, or the proposed intact-skin extension.
Restored-protein immunity across genodermatoses and clinical extension to severe ichthyoses or xeroderma pigmentosum are not established by these EB-focused sources.

The three-year, two-causal-gene and difficult-site thresholds are proposals; the supplied evidence does not establish a consensus threshold or the patient numbers needed to demonstrate reproducibility.

brief.title: Lasting repair for inherited skin disease
possible: People born with severe inherited skin disease could receive a single genetic treatment that keeps treated skin functioning as it renews itself. The treatment would correct stem cells, the long-lived cells that continually replace the skin’s surface.

Corrected cells could be grown into skin sheets and transplanted, or eventually treated inside the body. The goal is reliable repair across diseases caused by different genes, including hard-to-treat internal linings or skin that remains intact but functions poorly.
why: For people whose skin blisters and wounds under slight friction, lasting repair could reduce painful wounds and the daily burden of care. Correcting the cells that renew skin could also reduce dependence on repeated genetic treatment.

sources.showed: Koller reviewed clinical gene treatments for epidermolysis bullosa, an inherited blistering disease. Genetically corrected skin grafts provided lasting repair, while a gene-delivering gel improved wound healing with repeated application.
sources.quote: The transgenic epidermis is sustained by a defined number of regenerative epidermal stem cells, resulting in long-term clinical outcomes with no severe adverse effects reported to date.
sources.cited_for: Corrected stem cells can sustain functioning skin after transplantation.
sources.not_established: Reliable repair across different disease genes and difficult tissue sites remains to be demonstrated.

sources.who: Alex du Rand, Ben Buttle and Hilary Sheppard
sources.showed: Their review describes lasting local benefits from gene-corrected grafts and progress in gene editing, which changes DNA at chosen locations. Unintended DNA changes and delivery to the right cells remain barriers.
sources.quote:
We find that the widespread application
of Cas9 nuclease is currently hindered by off-target genotoxicity, which can be mitigated using Cas9 nickases.
sources.cited_for: Lasting local repair has clinical precedent, while gene editing still faces delivery and DNA-safety barriers.
sources.not_established: Broad clinical use still requires reliable correction of renewing cells and acceptable safety across disease genes.

sources.showed: This is a clinical trial of gene-corrected skin grafts for chronic wounds in recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, an inherited blistering disease.
sources.cited_for: Clinical testing of gene-corrected skin sheets for persistent wounds.
sources.not_established: The trial does not establish repair of internal linings or the whole body.

sources.who: Jean Tang and the Stanford Medicine-led trial team
sources.showed: In a trial involving 11 patients, wounds treated with genetically corrected skin grafts healed better and had less pain and itching than comparison wounds receiving usual care.
sources.quote: In addition, patients’ reports of pain, itching and blistering were better on the grafted areas than the control wounds, having shown more improvement from baseline.
sources.cited_for: Gene-corrected grafts can improve persistent wounds and symptoms in a small clinical trial.
sources.not_established: These local wound results leave long-term durability across other disease genes and tissue settings unresolved.

shown: Hirsch and colleagues regenerated skin using genetically corrected stem-cell grafts in a child with an inherited blistering disease. The grafts covered about 80% of the child’s body surface, demonstrating extensive local repair.

Stanford-led trials have also shown lasting wound-healing benefits from corrected skin sheets in another genetic form of the disease. The resulting graft therapy, Zevaskyn, has received approval for treating wounds.
missing: Reliable, lasting correction across diseases caused by different genes still needs demonstration.
Corrected stem cells must become established and persist in internal linings or intact, malfunctioning skin.
Treatment-specific DNA risks and the long-term behavior of corrected cell populations need assessment.

milestones.label: Lasting function across genetically distinct skin diseases
milestones.explanation: A single treatment would have to restore function for three years across distinct genetic diseases, including an internal lining or intact-skin disease. Persistent corrected stem cells would explain the lasting repair.

milestones.label: Independent patients and treatment preparations achieve sustained function
milestones.explanation: Lasting tissue function would have to recur across independent patients and separately prepared treatments, with successes and failures reported. This would establish reproducibility beyond isolated successes.

milestones.label: DNA changes and long-term treatment safety are assessed
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to assess unintended DNA changes, corrected cell populations over time, delivery complications and immune responses. These findings would establish the risks of each treatment approach.

milestones.label: Claims match demonstrated duration, reach and measured risks
milestones.explanation: Claims would have to reflect the treated tissues, patients, follow-up and risks the tests can detect. This would keep conclusions about durability and breadth within what the results establish.

uncertain: The proposed durability and disease-breadth thresholds lack consensus, and the patient numbers needed to establish reproducibility remain open.
How often would immune responses to a restored protein limit lasting repair across different inherited skin diseases?
Benefits in treated skin leave effects on disease elsewhere in the body unresolved.

page.title: One-time epidermal stem-cell gene therapy for durable local correction of inherited skin disease
page.definition: A single treatment would genetically correct a patient's epidermal stem cells, the long-lived cells that renew the skin's outer layer. The cells could be treated in the body or returned as sheets grown outside it. Their descendants would keep the treated tissue functional for years. The goal extends across diseases caused by different genes and includes treatment of mucosa or intact skin as well as open wounds.

goal.need: In a UK study, people with severe recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa spent a median of 18 hours a week changing dressings. A gene therapy gel for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa requires weekly application to wounds. If corrected stem cells keep renewing the skin, a treated site could resist blistering and remain less painful and itchy for years without repeat gene treatment. How much this eases daily wound care depends on how much affected skin heals.

completion.title: A single stem-cell gene treatment keeps tissue functional for 3 years in two genetic skin diseases.
completion.criterion: One corrective treatment of epidermal stem cells, ex vivo or in vivo, keeps treated tissue healed and free of blistering, or meets the disease's own functional measure, for at least 3 years with no further corrective treatment, in each of two severe inherited skin diseases caused by different genes. Each disease needs at least 3 patients given separately manufactured treatments, with treated area and failed sites stated in a peer-reviewed or regulator's report. Molecular analysis at 3 years or later shows corrected stem-cell clones maintaining the tissue. In at least one disease the treated site is mucosa or intact skin, not an open skin wound. Repeatedly applied therapy does not count.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas. The 3-year period, two causal genes, 3 patients per disease and the mucosal or intact-skin site come from this entry's record; no regulator or society defines when a one-time epidermal gene therapy counts as curative. The quoted review, published after ZEVASKYN was licensed, states that no permanent curative therapy exists.
completion.threshold_quote: In the absence of a permanent curative therapy for any EB subtype, treatment is palliative
completion.basis: The former test, a regulator's licence for a gene-modified epidermal graft in one genetic form of epidermolysis bullosa, is now milestone m4. That licence rests on wound healing and pain at 24 weeks and does not certify durable correction, a second causal gene or mucosal treatment. Three years establishes durability over that interval, not lifelong cure. Licensure is neither required nor sufficient. Whole-body correction and a single vector for every mutation are not asked for.

milestones.title: Corrected patient keratinocytes regenerate skin with the affected function restored in an animal model.
milestones.criterion: Graft corrected patient keratinocytes in a relevant animal model. Demonstrate regeneration of epidermis and restoration of the structure or function impaired by the mutation, using disease-appropriate comparisons. For an adhesion defect, assess the relevant protein at the junction between epidermis and dermis and the attachment structures it forms.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Human Gene Therapy for Rare Diseases, section IV, on the choice of model for in vivo proof of concept.
milestones.threshold_quote: should demonstrate a biological response to the investigational GT product that is similar to the expected response in humans.

milestones.title: An epidermal gene therapy graft engrafts and restores its missing adhesion protein in people.
milestones.criterion: In an authorised early-phase study of an epidermolysis bullosa adhesion defect, show that the graft takes and that the regenerated epidermis produces the deficient protein at the junction between epidermis and dermis. Assess tissue function and safety. For LAMB3 assess laminin-332 and epidermal attachment. For COL7A1 assess type VII collagen in graft-site biopsies and examine the anchoring fibrils that attach the epidermis to the dermis.
milestones.set_by: Clinical proof-of-concept convention in the LAMB3 phase I/II study and the registered COL7A1 phase 1/2a study, NCT01263379.
milestones.threshold_quote: Secondary endpoints included molecular correction as assessed by C7 expression by IIF and presence of C7 localizing to AFs by IEM

milestones.title: An RDEB graft improves both wound healing and dressing-change pain at 24 weeks versus matched controls.
milestones.criterion: In COL7A1 recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, randomize matched wounds within each patient to grafting or standard dressings. Both comparisons must favour grafting statistically at week 24: the proportion of wounds at least 50% healed from baseline, confirmed at least two weeks later, and the mean reduction from baseline in wound pain within three hours after a dressing change. VIITAL used the 0–10 Wong-Baker FACES scale, with a numerical rating scale before protocol version 6.
milestones.set_by: FDA, ZEVASKYN Summary Basis for Regulatory Action, accepting the VIITAL co-primary endpoints.
milestones.threshold_quote: The co-primary endpoints were wound healing and pain reduction at Week 24.

milestones.title: A regulator licenses a gene-modified epidermal graft for one genetic form of epidermolysis bullosa.
milestones.criterion: A regulator licenses a patient's own epidermal sheets, genetically modified outside the body to produce the deficient adhesion protein, for treating wounds in a genetically specified form of epidermolysis bullosa. The approval identifies the product, the disease and the sites covered by the indication.
milestones.set_by: FDA, biologics licence application 125807, ZEVASKYN approval letter.
milestones.threshold_quote: Under this license, you are authorized to manufacture the product prademagene zamikeracel

milestones.title: One graft treatment keeps skin functional for 3 years, sustained by corrected stem-cell clones.
milestones.criterion: In one severe inherited skin disease, a single application of genetically corrected epidermal grafts keeps the treated skin healed and free of blistering for at least 3 years with no further corrective treatment in at least one patient, in a peer-reviewed report. Integration-site or equivalent molecular analysis shows that corrected stem-cell clones maintain the regenerated epidermis. A second causal gene, mucosa and intact skin are not required.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas; the completion test's durability and clonal evidence without its breadth. The quoted editorial describes the junctional epidermolysis bullosa grafts in these terms; no outside body sets the period.
milestones.threshold_quote: The transgenic epidermis is sustained by a defined number of regenerative epidermal stem cells, resulting in long-term clinical outcomes with no severe adverse effects reported to date.

milestones.title: Genetic correction restores the affected function in cultured patient keratinocytes.
milestones.criterion: Show that cultured keratinocytes from a patient regain the function impaired by the causal mutation after genetic correction. For LAMB3 deficiency, assess adhesion and the ability to form colonies. For another gene, use a functional readout of its defect.
milestones.set_by: FDA rare-disease gene therapy guidance recommends in vitro proof of concept. The disease-specific readout follows the patient-cell studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: Preclinical in vitro and in vivo proof-of-concept (POC) studies are recommended

milestones.title: Preclinical evidence supports the proposed starting dose and route for a first human treatment.
milestones.criterion: Characterize the product's distribution and potential local and systemic toxicity under conditions relevant to the planned clinical route, dose range and schedule. Use the findings to justify the starting dose and identify what the clinical study should monitor.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Human Gene Therapy for Rare Diseases, section IV, on the objectives of the preclinical programme.
milestones.threshold_quote: establishment of feasibility and reasonable safety of the proposed clinical route of administration

milestones.title: A LAMB3 junctional EB graft meets the Hologene 5 definition of transplant success at 12 months.
milestones.criterion: At 12 months, score each transplant on two measures: the extent of blister-free re-epithelialization and evidence of functional, genetically corrected epidermis from laboratory and mechanical assessments. A transplant succeeds if it meets both criteria. If it meets exactly one, success requires a positive patient-reported assessment of the treated area. If it meets neither, it fails. Report the proportion of successful transplants.
milestones.set_by: Hologene 5 protocol, EudraCT 2018-000261-36, primary endpoint and Figure 2.
milestones.threshold_quote: Percentage of transplantation scored as success at the 12-month follow-up based on the definition of success using the 2-step rule

not_found: No externally set test combining a cross-genodermatosis cure, three years of durability, two causal genes and a mucosal or intact-skin result was located in regulatory, society or trial documents.
No common follow-up duration certifying lifelong correction was located.
The FDA summary did not disclose the number of mice underlying its reported preclinical graft-persistence results.
No regulator or professional society statement rejecting the feasibility or value of durable local stem-cell correction in epidermolysis bullosa was located.

references.title: Final Publishable Summary Report — GENEGRAFT
Topline results from EB-101 pivotal phase 3 VIITAL™ study

results.finding: In VIITAL, 81% of grafted RDEB wounds were at least half healed at week 24 across 43 matched wound pairs in 11 patients.
results.detail: The release attributes the result to the peer-reviewed Lancet trial. It does not give the pain scale or endpoint-specific statistical results.
results.quote: At 24 weeks after grafting, 81% of treated wounds were at least half healed, compared with 16% of control wounds.

results.finding: The FDA approved the autologous gene-modified graft on April 29. The associated RDEB trial enrolled 11 patients.
results.detail: The source is Stanford Medicine’s announcement of the FDA action. It supplies neither the FDA decision nor the approved label.
results.quote:
The skin grafts were
granted approval
as an EB therapy on April 29 by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

results.finding: In the six-donor LAMB3 JEB study, corrected keratinocytes recovered normal growth kinetics in a 4-day culture assay.
results.detail: The holoclone experiment measured how many isolated colonies carried the transferred gene. It did not measure whether correction improved the ability to form colonies.
results.quote:
We found that β3 gene
 delivery, but not GFP, resulted in the restoration of cellular
 morphology and short-term growth kinetics to that of normal controls

results.finding: LAMB3-corrected keratinocytes from six patients regenerated epidermis with hemidesmosomes in SCID mice, with β3 expression through 8 weeks.
results.detail: Electron microscopy showed hemidesmosomes in corrected grafts and their absence in β3-negative controls. The 8-week measurement refers to β3 expression.
results.quote:
Tissue regenerated from β3-transduced JEB keratinocytes produced
 phenotypically normal skin characterized by sustained β3 expression
 and the formation of hemidesmosomes.

results.finding: Transduced RDEB keratinocytes expressed type VII collagen in culture. Donor count and expression level were unspecified.
results.detail: The six-donor sample in the report belongs to a separate integration-site analysis.
results.quote:
In vitro pharmacology studies demonstrated that human keratinocytes obtained from 
healthy donors and donors with RDEB transduced with the RVV and vectors similar to 
the RVV expressed Col7 protein.

results.finding: Human keratinocyte grafts in mouse wounds expressed type VII collagen for up to 12 months. Mouse count was unspecified.
results.quote:
RVV-transduced keratinocytes remained 
localized within explanted nonclinical products, and RVV-mediated expression of Col7 
was detected for up to 12-months post-implantation.

results.finding: In mice with representative grafts, vector was below detection outside the graft at assessments through 8 weeks. Mouse count was unspecified.
results.detail: The study used transduced cells on a dermal matrix. The clinical product consists of epidermal sheets applied to wound beds.
results.quote:
COL7A1 transgene DNA 
was detected in explanted nonclinical products at both sacrifice time points.

results.finding: Graft-site biopsies detected type VII collagen and anchoring fibrils in 6 of 7 RDEB patients at 3 months.
results.detail: At 3 months, 94.7% of treated chronic wounds and 33.3% of unmatched control wounds had healed by at least 50%. Circulating anti-collagen antibodies in two patients resolved without intervention by one year.
results.quote:
In the Phase 1/2a study (n=7), the NC2 domain of Col7 protein and anchoring fibrils 
were detected in biopsies from 6 treated subjects at 3 months and in 5 treated subjects 
at 6 months.

results.finding: VIITAL randomized 86 wounds in 11 RDEB patients. Grafting increased the week-24 rate of at least 50% healing by 65.1 percentage points.
results.detail: The report gives the Wong-Baker FACES result and its statistical significance. The criterion also requires measurement within three hours after a dressing change.
results.quote:
At week 24, a 
higher proportion of ZEVASKYN treated wounds (81.4%) achieved ≥50% healing from 
baseline compared to control wounds (16.3%; p<0.0001).

results.finding: The FDA documents approval of 1 autologous COL7A1 epidermal graft for RDEB wounds in adults and children.
results.quote:
This document summarizes the basis of approval of ZEVASKYN for treatment of wounds 
in recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (RDEB).

results.finding: In 1 patient with LAMB3 junctional EB, grafted skin showed restored junctional laminin-332 and epidermal attachment at 6.5 years.
results.quote:
In contrast, control and trans-
genic epidermis expressed virtually identical amounts
of laminin 332- b3, which was properly located at the
epidermal-dermal junction ( Figures 2 A and 2B).

results.finding: In 1 patient with severe LAMB3 junctional EB, grafted skin stayed functional and blister-free for 6.5 years and was sustained by corrected stem-cell clones.
results.detail: Blistering persisted around the treated area. The authors inferred long-term clonal maintenance from the integration-site analysis and widespread vector-derived LAMB3 expression in the regenerated epidermis.
results.quote:
During the 6.5-year follow-up, the epidermis of both of
Claudio’s upper legs was normal looking, normally pig-
mented, and robust, and did not itch or form blisters, either
spontaneously or after induced mechanical stress (such as
biopsy withdrawal).

results.finding: One child with LAMB3 junctional EB had normal laminin 332 and functional grafted epidermis at 5 years.
results.detail: The protocol attributes the detailed follow-up to a submitted manuscript.
results.quote: At the last follow-up (5years after transplantation), the patient’s newly formed epidermis expressed normal levels of laminin 332, had an intact basement membrane

results.finding: One adult with LAMB3 junctional EB retained stable transgenic epidermis at 16 years.
results.detail: The 16-year update reports graft stability and safety. The protocol discusses stem-cell clone evidence separately.
results.quote: An ongoing observational study confirms both the stability of the transgenic epidermis and the absence of AEs 16years after transplantation.

results.finding: In 7 adults with RDEB, type VII collagen NC2 was detected in 73% of graft-site biopsies at 3 months.
results.quote: The NC2 domain of C7 was detected in 73% (11 of 15) of biopsies at 3 months, in 53% (8 of 15) of biopsies at 6 months, in 11% (1 of 9) of biopsies at 1 year, and 67% (2 of 3) at 2 years.

results.finding: In 7 adults with RDEB, 36 of 38 evaluable grafted wounds reached at least 50% healing at 6 months.
results.detail: Pain was assessed as present or absent at treated sites during study visits.
results.quote:
Wound healing of 50% or greater by IGA was present in 95% (36 of 38) of treated wounds versus 0% (0 of 6) of untreated control wounds at 6 months (
P
< 0.0001).

results.finding: In the 7-adult RDEB study, 80% of evaluable treated sites were at least 50% healed at 3 years.
results.detail: Twenty sites were evaluable at year 3. The report documents type VII collagen expression through year 2.
results.quote:
As seen in
Figures 2
and
3
, at 3 and 6 months, 95% (36 of 38) of treated sites had 50% or greater healing, compared with 68% (26 of 38) at 12 months, 71% (27 of 38) at 2 years, and 80% (16 of 20) at 3 years.

results.finding: In seven adults with RDEB, 39 of 42 EB-101 graft sites showed at least 50% healing at six months.
results.detail: The anchoring fibril findings in Table 1 are from baseline biopsies.
results.quote:
Six months after 
application, 92.9% (39/42) of grafted sites achieved ≥ 50% 
wound healing.

results.finding: In seven adults with RDEB, 39 of 42 EB-101 graft sites reached the 50% healing threshold at six months.
results.detail: The later pain survey used a seven-point ordinal scale for change from baseline.
results.quote:
Six months after 
application, 92.9% (39/42) of grafted sites achieved ≥ 50% 
wound healing.

results.finding: In a seven-adult RDEB cohort, 21 of 30 assessed EB-101 graft sites showed at least 50% healing at year five.
results.detail: Serial biopsies for full-length type VII collagen ended at year two. At year five, blistering was assessed as a change in susceptibility after trauma.
results.quote:
At year five, 70% (21/30) of treated sites demonstrated ≥ 50% wound healing compared to baseline 
by investigator global assessment.

results.finding: In transduced RDEB keratinocytes, integration-site analysis found no site preference. The sample size was unstated.
results.detail: The reported distribution is across the host genome. The criterion calls for distribution of the administered product.
results.quote:
Integration site analysis in RDEB 
keratinocytes transduced with LZRSE-Col7A1 showed a low level of integration distributed throughout the host 
genome with no predilection to specific integration sites, including in genes associated with malignant 
transformation in humans.

results.finding: In the 7-patient RDEB graft study, 6 patients had both type VII collagen NC2 and anchoring fibrils at month 3.
results.detail: NC2 was assessed by immunofluorescence and anchoring fibrils by immunoelectron microscopy.
results.quote:
The NC2 domain of C7 and AFs were detected in 6 patients at 3 
months and in 5 patients at 6 months.

results.finding: VIITAL randomized 86 wounds in 11 RDEB patients. At month 6, 81% of grafted wounds reached at least 50% healing.
results.detail: One control wound lacked a baseline pain score and was excluded from the pain analysis.

results.finding: The FDA approved ZEVASKYN for RDEB wounds in 2025. The supporting VIITAL study enrolled 11 patients.
results.quote:
ZEVASKYN (prademagene zamikeracel), gene-modified cellular sheets, 
for topical use 
Initial U.S. Approval:  2025

results.finding: The Hologene 5 LAMB3 junctional EB study reported zero serious adverse events among two participants in the safety set.
results.detail: The study ended prematurely. The 12-month transplant-success endpoint was unevaluable in both participants, so the registry gives no transplant-success proportion.
results.quote: No serious adverse events were reported during the study.

results.finding: FDA issued 1 biologics license for ZEVASKYN to treat wounds in adults and children with RDEB.
results.detail: The unit is a regulatory approval. A patient sample size does not apply.
results.quote:
Under this license, you are authorized to manufacture the product prademagene 
zamikeracel, which is indicated for treatment of wounds in adult and pediatric patients 
with recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (RDEB).

results.finding: In VIITAL (11 patients, 43 grafted wounds), week-24 wound pain improved more with pz-cel than with control treatment (p=0.0002).
results.detail: The poster cites the peer-reviewed VIITAL primary report as the source of the week-24 result.
results.quote:
In the phase 3 trial, the mean change from baseline to week 
24 in wound pain was –3.07 with pz-cel and –0.90 in 
controls (p=0.0002).

results.finding: After one pz-cel grafting procedure in 11 patients with 43 treated wounds, the poster reports sustained wound healing through month 60.
results.detail: The poster provides representative wound images and site-level healing assessments. It gives no molecular clonal analysis.
results.quote:
At months 12, 18, 24, 30 and up 
to Month 60 post-treatment, a 
great proportion of treated 
wounds demonstrated sustained 
efficacy following a one-time 
surgical application of pz-cel.

results.finding: In one patient with LAMB3 junctional EB, sampled grafted skin showed no clinical blistering at 72 months.
results.detail: The 72-month study sampled selected skin sites for microbiome analysis. The paper attributes the earlier 5-year assessment of the entire grafted epidermis to previous publications.
results.quote: Despite this dysbiosis, transgenic areas remained stable and showed no clinical signs of eczema or blistering.

results.finding: Keratinocytes from one LAMB3 JEB patient regained colony formation after correction. In the adhesion assay, 20 corrected clones and 10 controls were tested, with corrected cells detaching at ~16 min.
results.detail: Colony formation was assessed qualitatively by microscopy of two representative corrected clones grown on a feeder layer.
results.quote: The detachment time for LAMB3-expressing clones was comparable to normal keratinocytes (16 min), and negative clones as well as JEB.A649fsX38 cells detached after 5 min of trypsin treatment

results.finding: Gene-edited COL17A1 JEB keratinocytes from one patient adhered significantly better to laminin-332 than untreated cells (assay n = 3).
results.detail: Adhesion improved across the tested editing conditions. The bulk-cell assay could not isolate the contribution of precise repair from that of reading-frame restoration. Colony-forming capacity declined after editing.
results.quote: Adhesion analysis revealed higher adhesive strength of RNP and ± ssODN-treated primary JEB keratinocytes to laminin-332 compared to untreated JEB control.

results.finding: Cultured keratinocytes from one KRT14 EB simplex patient regained sheet cohesion after editing, with fewer fragments under mechanical stress (N = 3, p < 0.05).
results.detail: The sheet assay compared edited patient cells with untreated cells from the same patient and with healthy-donor cells. The reported p value compares edited and untreated patient sheets.
results.quote:
In contrast, high-
force stress induced fragmentation of EBS01 but not
NHEK and eEBS01 sheets (D).

results.finding: Corrected RDEB patient keratinocytes regenerated skin that resisted suction-induced separation at 12 weeks in immunodeficient mice (n=2 per group).
results.detail: The mouse count applies to the suction test. The text does not specify the total number of mice assessed for histology or electron microscopy.
results.quote: No blistering was apparent on 12-week grafts from sg2 + sg3 RNP-treated patient keratinocytes

results.finding: Nude-mouse skin grafts from corrected KRT14 p.R125H patient keratinocytes had spontaneous blistering in 0 of 7 grafts.
results.detail: The endpoint was spontaneous blistering at 8 weeks. The supplied text reports no mechanical challenge.
results.quote:
Three transplants derived from EBDM‐1 keratinocytes (from a total of 11 transplants) demonstrated spontaneous blistering, whereas EBDM‐1+RV_RTM163_GFP‐derived transplants (
n
= 7) revealed a phenotype like the control grafts (hKc; human wild‐type keratinocyte derived,
n
= 11), showing no signs of any blister formation

results.finding: Nude mice (n unreported) developed no tumors after subcutaneous injection of 2 million COL7A1-corrected RDEB keratinocytes and fibroblasts.
results.detail: The subcutaneous injection was a separate tumorigenicity study. The route-relevant graft study reported favorable tolerability and preliminary organ DNA results, with graft dose and group sizes unreported.
results.quote:
The subcutaneous tumorigenicity study showed that nude mice developed no tumour, were healthy 
with normal weight curves 80 days after subcutaneous inj ection of 2.106 of genetically engineered 
RDEB keratinocytes and fibroblasts.

results.finding: In VIITAL, EB-101 improved week-24 dressing-change pain in 11 COL7A1 RDEB patients (42 matched wound pairs), with a mean pairwise benefit of 2.23 points.
results.detail: The webcast does not establish whether controls received standard dressings or whether pain was assessed within three hours after a dressing change.
results.quote:
The mean pairwise 
difference across patients 
in pain reduction was 2.23 
with p=0.0002 and sample 
size of 42 wound pairs in 
11 patients.

Reason: Rewritten by Claude Fable 5.2 at the owner's request, 16 November 2026, under the completed-breakthrough standard. The title named a class of treatment that one licensed product satisfies. The record's breakthrough is a one-time cure through the stem-cell compartment across disease genes; the title now says so.

definition = "A patient's epidermal stem cells, the long-lived cells that renew the skin's outer layer, are genetically corrected once, in transplanted sheets or inside the body, so that treated tissue stays functional for years without repeat treatment. The capability holds for inherited skin diseases caused by different genes, and in mucosa or intact skin as well as open wounds.". Reason: Rewritten by Claude Fable 5.2 at the owner's request, 16 November 2026, under the completed-breakthrough standard. The definition described treating selected wounds in one disorder. It now states the durability and breadth that the record defines.

edit completion: title = "A single stem-cell gene treatment keeps tissue functional for 3 years in two genetic skin diseases."; criterion = "One corrective treatment of epidermal stem cells, ex vivo or in vivo, keeps treated tissue healed and free of blistering, or meets the disease's own functional measure, for at least 3 years with no further corrective treatment, in each of two severe inherited skin diseases caused by different genes. Each disease needs at least 3 patients given separately manufactured treatments, with treated area and failed sites stated in a peer-reviewed or regulator's report. Molecular analysis at 3 years or later shows corrected stem-cell clones maintaining the tissue. In at least one disease the treated site is mucosa or intact skin, not an open skin wound. Repeatedly applied therapy does not count."; set_by = "Technology Atlas. The 3-year period, two causal genes, 3 patients per disease and the mucosal or intact-skin site come from this entry's record; no regulator or society defines when a one-time epidermal gene therapy counts as curative. The quoted review, published after ZEVASKYN was licensed, states that no permanent curative therapy exists."; set_by_kind = "atlas"; threshold_quote = "In the absence of a permanent curative therapy for any EB subtype, treatment is palliative"; threshold_ref = 101; basis = "The former test, a regulator's licence for a gene-modified epidermal graft in one genetic form of epidermolysis bullosa, is now milestone m4. That licence rests on wound healing and pain at 24 weeks and does not certify durable correction, a second causal gene or mucosal treatment. Three years establishes durability over that interval, not lifelong cure. Licensure is neither required nor sufficient. Whole-body correction and a single vector for every mutation are not asked for."; refs = [101, 3, 6, 7]. Reason: Rewritten by Claude Fable 5.2 at the owner's request, 16 November 2026, under the completed-breakthrough standard. The test was FDA licensure of one graft product for wounds in one form of epidermolysis bullosa, on a 24-week endpoint. The record's own completion criteria ask for three-year function from one treatment in two diseases of different causal genes, persistent corrected clones and a mucosal or intact-skin site; the test now states them.

title = "One-time epidermal stem-cell gene therapy for durable local correction of inherited skin disease". Reason: The completion test establishes a defined period of function at treated sites, while the current title implies a cure of the patient's disease.

definition = "A single treatment would genetically correct a patient's epidermal stem cells, the long-lived cells that renew the skin's outer layer. The cells could be treated in the body or returned as sheets grown outside it. Their descendants would keep the treated tissue functional for years. The goal extends across diseases caused by different genes and includes treatment of mucosa or intact skin as well as open wounds.". Reason: The definition presents the intended breadth as an existing capability and leaves unclear what a one-time treatment corrects.

goal.need = "In a UK study, people with severe recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa spent a median of 18 hours a week changing dressings. A gene therapy gel for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa requires weekly application to wounds. If corrected stem cells keep renewing the skin, a treated site could resist blistering and remain less painful and itchy for years without repeat gene treatment. How much this eases daily wound care depends on how much affected skin heals.". Reason: Time spent on wound care and symptoms reported at healed sites explain the value of durable correction more directly than the length of an epidermal renewal cycle.

add statement by GENEGRAFT consortium, European Union Seventh Framework Programme, 2018: "ex vivo gene therapy approach for a permanent treatment of RDEB.". Reason: GENEGRAFT explicitly named permanent local treatment as its objective for the COL7A1 disorder.

add not found: "No regulator or professional society statement rejecting the feasibility or value of durable local stem-cell correction in epidermolysis bullosa was located.". Reason: The available society and regulatory statements distinguish uncertainty about an investigational treatment from a judgment against the goal.
add case "COL17A1 junctional EB". Reason: HOLOGENE17 registered a human epidermal stem-cell graft study specifically for collagen XVII deficiency.
add case "KRT14 EB simplex". Reason: KRT14 epidermolysis bullosa simplex has a distinct dominant disease mechanism and published preclinical studies of genetically modified patient keratinocytes.

add milestone after None: "Genetic correction restores the affected function in cultured patient keratinocytes.". Reason: Correction of the defect in cultured patient cells is demonstrable before an animal graft is attempted.

edit m1: title = "Corrected patient keratinocytes regenerate skin with the affected function restored in an animal model."; criterion = "Graft corrected patient keratinocytes in a relevant animal model. Demonstrate regeneration of epidermis and restoration of the structure or function impaired by the mutation, using disease-appropriate comparisons. For an adhesion defect, assess the relevant protein at the junction between epidermis and dermis and the attachment structures it forms."; set_by = "FDA, Human Gene Therapy for Rare Diseases, section IV, on the choice of model for in vivo proof of concept."; threshold_quote = "should demonstrate a biological response to the investigational GT product that is similar to the expected response in humans."; threshold_ref = 8; refs = [8, 2, 7, 22]. Reason: Animal proof of concept tests whether corrected cells regenerate functional skin, a question distinct from dose safety and applicable to defects beyond missing adhesion proteins.

add milestone after m1: "Preclinical evidence supports the proposed starting dose and route for a first human treatment.". Reason: The original animal milestone also required biodistribution and toxicology evidence, which FDA evaluates for a different purpose from tissue regeneration.

edit m2: criterion = "In an authorised early-phase study of an epidermolysis bullosa adhesion defect, show that the graft takes and that the regenerated epidermis produces the deficient protein at the junction between epidermis and dermis. Assess tissue function and safety. For LAMB3 assess laminin-332 and epidermal attachment. For COL7A1 assess type VII collagen in graft-site biopsies and examine the anchoring fibrils that attach the epidermis to the dermis."; set_by = "Clinical proof-of-concept convention in the LAMB3 phase I/II study and the registered COL7A1 phase 1/2a study, NCT01263379."; threshold_quote = "Secondary endpoints included molecular correction as assessed by C7 expression by IIF and presence of C7 localizing to AFs by IEM"; threshold_ref = 13; refs = [9, 13, 7]. Reason: The early human test needs the graft-site examination and molecular readout in place of a recital of patient outcomes.

edit m3: title = "An RDEB graft improves both wound healing and dressing-change pain at 24 weeks versus matched controls."; criterion = "In COL7A1 recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, randomize matched wounds within each patient to grafting or standard dressings. Both comparisons must favour grafting statistically at week 24: the proportion of wounds at least 50% healed from baseline, confirmed at least two weeks later, and the mean reduction from baseline in wound pain within three hours after a dressing change. VIITAL used the 0\u201310 Wong-Baker FACES scale, with a numerical rating scale before protocol version 6."; set_by = "FDA, ZEVASKYN Summary Basis for Regulatory Action, accepting the VIITAL co-primary endpoints."; threshold_quote = "The co-primary endpoints were wound healing and pain reduction at Week 24."; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7, 1, 24]. Reason: VIITAL specifies an RDEB test with paired wounds, confirmed healing and pain assessed after a dressing change.

add milestone after m3: "A LAMB3 junctional EB graft meets the Hologene 5 definition of transplant success at 12 months.". Reason: Hologene 5 defined a separate 12-month test for a successful LAMB3 graft, and the registry reports that its primary endpoint could be evaluated in no participant.

edit m4: criterion = "A regulator licenses a patient's own epidermal sheets, genetically modified outside the body to produce the deficient adhesion protein, for treating wounds in a genetically specified form of epidermolysis bullosa. The approval identifies the product, the disease and the sites covered by the indication."; set_by = "FDA, biologics licence application 125807, ZEVASKYN approval letter."; threshold_quote = "Under this license, you are authorized to manufacture the product prademagene zamikeracel"; threshold_ref = 6; refs = [6, 1, 7]. Reason: The scope of the licensed indication determines whether a graft meets this milestone, independently of the Atlas revision date.
structure = parallel. Reason: The pivotal endpoints apply to different gene-defined disorders, and long-term evidence from an early graft can precede both a pivotal trial and licensure.
remove not found 2. Reason: The full VIITAL paper is available and reports both co-primary endpoints, so the earlier page-access errors no longer identify a gap in the evidence.
